title: The safety scan: look before you move
outcomes: Names the two scan questions and runs them before a move
Finds loose pieces on both sides of the board
Explains why a defended piece can still be unsafe
Runs the scan without being prompted in a silent item

steps.text:
The **safety scan** is the two questions from the threat lesson, run on every move in about ten seconds.
**1. What did my opponent's last move threaten or open?**
**2. Is any of my pieces loose, or attacked by something cheaper?**
This is a habit to try, not a law. It catches obvious dangers, not deep ones.

steps.caption: White to move. Run the scan before anything else.

line.say: The bishop on e4 is attacked by the knight and nothing defends it. Bxf6 takes that attacker.

claims.statement: The bishop on e4 is loose.
One Black piece attacks the bishop on e4.
One Black piece attacks the bishop on g5 (the h6 pawn).
Bxf6 is the engine's best move.

steps.text:
**Defended is not the same as safe.** A defended piece that a *cheaper* piece attacks can still be lost: the cheaper piece takes, you retake, and you gave up more than you won.
Ask: **is it attacked, and what would the trade cost me?**
The scan also works the other way. Your opponent's loose pieces are chances.

steps.title: Same square, different attacker
steps.prompt: A rook attacks a defended knight. Then a pawn does. Predict, for each, whether White must react.

steps.text: **What the app does for you now, and when it stops.** Here the two scan questions sit beside the board. In mixed practice they are hidden; you can open them and the app notes that you did. The plan: stop showing them once you solve five mixed items in a row with them closed (five is a first guess). Next item is silent: no prompts, hints or engine.

steps.prompt: That item was silent. Before you moved, did you run the two scan questions without being told to? Answer honestly: this record is for you, not a grade.

fields.label: Did you run the scan before moving?
What did the scan show? (one line)
In your next real game, on which moves will you run the scan on purpose?
